statements.proposition: This change keeps existing string-based edge conditions working as before (backward compatible) while adding callable conditions.
statements.label: FALSE
statements.note: Settled by reading head vs base code; could not run the code (sandboxed install with network was denied by the permission system, so no tests were executed). In DiGraph.has_cycles_with_exit the exit-condition test changed from `any(edge.condition ...)` (truthy for string conditions) to `any(edge.condition_function is not None ...)`, and string conditions never set condition_function. A cyclic graph whose only exit is a string condition (the existing pattern, e.g. C->A condition='exit', and the PR's own test_cycle_detection_with_exit_condition / loop builder tests) previously validated and now raises ValueError 'Cycle detected without exit condition'. Also the mixed conditional/unconditional validation no longer counts string conditions as conditional, and add_conditional_edges now builds lambdas whose condition is set to None on the model, so string-keyed conditions are lost from edge.condition/serialization. These are concrete behaviour changes for existing string conditions.
evidence: gh api pulls/6565/files: only 3 files modified: _digraph_group_chat.py, _graph_builder.py, tests/test_group_chat_graph.py

Head checkout of _digraph_group_chat.py lines ~155: `if not any(edge.condition_function is not None for edge in cycle_edges): raise ValueError("Cycle detected without exit condition...")`; diff shows base was `any(edge.condition for edge in cycle_edges)`
_validate_condition only sets condition_function when condition is callable, so string conditions leave condition_function None
Diff of _graph_builder.py add_conditional_edges: now passes a lambda to add_edge instead of the condition string; callable condition is set to None by the validator
